assessments.label: CPU utilisation
assessments.finding: Average CPU 88.0% (p95 100.0%, peak 100.0%); saturated (>=90%) in 50.0% of samples.
assessments.impact: Increased search latency, event processing delays and risk of event drops at the pipeline.
assessments.root_cause: Event processing (ecs-ep / ecs-ec-ingress), Ariel searches, CRE rule evaluation or application containers are consuming available CPU capacity.
recommendation: Identify the processes with the highest CPU (ecs-ec-ingress, ecs-ep, ariel_proxy_server, postgres, java/tomcat, apps).
Review custom rules (CRE) and expensive custom properties; disable or optimise those that are CPU-heavy.
Redistribute event sources or add an Event/Flow Processor; consider upgrading appliance hardware.
assessments.best_practice: IBM sizing guidance targets sustained CPU below 70% with peaks below 90%.

assessments.label: CPU I/O wait
assessments.impact: Indicates storage latency or contention; delays event commit and search execution.
assessments.root_cause: CPU threads are blocked waiting for storage; usually slow disks, heavy Ariel searches or retention/cleanup jobs.
recommendation: Review storage subsystem health and latency.
Reduce concurrent heavy Ariel searches/reports; review retention.
assessments.best_practice: Sustained iowait above 10% is a sign of storage contention.

assessments.label: Memory utilisation
assessments.impact: Swapping drastically reduces performance of PostgreSQL, ECS and Java processes and can trigger OOM kills.
assessments.root_cause: Large resident sets from Java (tomcat/ecs), PostgreSQL shared buffers or application containers; insufficient RAM for the assigned roles.
recommendation: Identify top memory processes and heap settings (tomcat, ecs, postgres); restart leaking processes in a change window.
Add RAM or relocate applications/services to another host.
Check that no unsupported software is installed on the appliance.
assessments.best_practice: Keep swap usage near 0% and available memory above 10% of total.

assessments.label: Swap usage
assessments.impact: Performance degradation and indicates memory sizing problems.
assessments.root_cause: Memory demand exceeded physical RAM, forcing the kernel to page out.
recommendation: Review memory consumers and consider memory upgrade.
Verify swap activity with 'sar -W' and tune application memory limits.
assessments.best_practice: Swap activity should be negligible during normal operation.

assessments.label: Load average (5 min)
assessments.impact: Runnable queue backlog results in scheduling delays for all services.
assessments.root_cause: More runnable/blocked tasks than CPU cores; CPU or I/O contention.
recommendation: Identify CPU/IO bound tasks using top and iostat.
Reduce concurrent searches/report generation; consider more cores.
assessments.best_practice: Sustained load average should remain below the number of cores.

assessments.label: httpd worker count
assessments.impact: Excessive memory usage and UI sluggishness; possible 503 errors.
assessments.root_cause: Heavy concurrent UI/API/app-proxy requests or slow backend responses holding workers open.
recommendation: Review API clients and integrations polling the Console; throttle automation.
Check for slow/hung backend services (tomcat, ariel_proxy).
assessments.best_practice: Keep httpd worker counts stable; investigate sustained growth.

assessments.label: Disk usage /
assessments.best_practice: IBM recommends keeping /store below 80% with retention aligned to compliance; never run above 90% as the 95% hard stop halts processing.
